title: Quiet Compute
campaign_line: Data centers are too freaking loud.
research_question: Can a declared compute system reduce acoustic output under the same useful workload while satisfying thermal, energy, water, reliability, cost, uncertainty, and independent-reproduction constraints?

scope.version_0_1_boundary: One declared server or rack under a repeatable compute workload in a documented acoustic and thermal environment.

milestones.title: Measurement contract
milestones.exit_evidence: Machine-validated measurement, passport, deliberate-submission, comparison, and adversarial-test contracts exist; external domain review and preregistration remain required.

milestones.title: Controlled baseline
milestones.exit_evidence: Repeated acoustic, workload, thermal, energy, and environment traces for one declared system.

milestones.title: Independent baseline reproduction
milestones.exit_evidence: A separate operator recovers the baseline within preregistered tolerance.

milestones.title: One bounded intervention
milestones.exit_evidence: One control, airflow, liquid-cooling, or thermal-material change improves acoustics without failing a guardrail.

milestones.title: Secure distributed runner
milestones.exit_evidence: Ed25519 admission, capability filtering, diversity allocation, tolerance consensus, replay checks, and fail-closed isolation plans exist; execution remains disabled pending an independently reviewed sandbox adapter.

milestones.title: Partner-led materials search
milestones.exit_evidence: A domain expert, experimental partner, validated solver stack, and unique licensed dataset exist.
